subject: Evaluation playbook & security scope — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Evaluation playbook & security scope — next steps

Lena — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Buyers & roles (as discussed): Marcus Reed is the economic buyer; you (Lena) are the technical owner for the pilot; Procurement will own contract & PO.
- Decision criteria we heard: end-to-end latency target (~<200ms for typical prompt), predictable unit cost (target below your current baseline), and a private/VPC deployment option for PHI-sensitive subsystems.
- Security/legal/procurement asks: Solstice will need a SOC 2 attestation, data flow diagram for inference traffic, and answers to a vendor security questionnaire (standard RFI).

Proposed next steps: 
1) I’ll send our security intake workbook (asks + evidence checklist) by EOD Fri (attached: 20261202-postcall-notes.txt as quick notes).
2) Can you confirm which systems must be in-scope for the security review (prod API, analytics stack, partner SFTP, etc.) so we can tailor the questionnaire?
3) We’ll propose a 30–45min kickoff with our security lead (Karthik) once you return the initial scope.

If it helps, I’ve copied Ben (solutions engineer) and Karthik will join the kickoff to walk the intake workbook.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0183

Attachment: 20261202-postcall-notes.txt (text)
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@solsticehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Reed <mreed@solsticehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation playbook & security scope — next steps

Marissa — thanks for the notes and for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side before the kickoff: 

- In-scope systems we anticipate: 
  * Production inference API (prod cluster behind our API GW)
  * Orchestration layer (Kubernetes cluster hosting inference workers)
  * Minimal integration surface (our tenant DB is out-of-scope for initial pilot)
  * Analytics pipeline and partner SFTP likely out-of-scope for phase 1 but we’ll confirm.

- Our legal/procurement team needs to review any standard DPA language early — I’m copying Marcus so Procurement can be looped in.

Could you send the security intake workbook and a short template for the data-flow diagram? Also confirm whether Redwood needs any on-prem connection or if a VPC peering option will be sufficient for pilot traffic.

Appreciate it — Lena

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@solsticehealth.com>, Marcus Reed <mreed@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation playbook & security scope — next steps

Hi Lena / Marcus — Karthik from Redwood Security & Onboarding here. Thanks for the clear scope notes, that helps. A few practical items to move this forward: 

1) I’ve attached our security intake workbook (Redwood-security-intake-v2.xlsx) and a simple data-flow template (data-flow-template.png). Please fill the top-level sheet with which systems you want in-scope for the pilot (we can iterate after kickoff).

2) Recommended initial scope for fastest path: 
   - INCLUDE: Production inference API (prod), inference orchestration (K8s), authentication layer (OIDC), and any external egress endpoints used for model downloads.
   - EXCLUDE (for phase 1 to speed review): analytics pipelines, historical data lakes, partner SFTP endpoints — we can add these for a later phase if desired.

3) Evidence we typically collect during intake: SOC 2 Type II report (if available), network diagram, encryption at rest (AES-256) and in-transit (TLS 1.2+) policies, access control + RBAC screenshots, and a short runbook for incident response. We can accept consolidated artifacts in a shared Drive link or as attachments — whatever works for you.

4) Procurement / legal notes: if you require a DPA review, please send the version you prefer; our legal team can do a cursory review prior to contracting. If an NDA is needed before sharing sensitive diagrams, we can surface a standard mutual NDA quickly.

5) Proposed kickoff slots (30–45m): 
   - Tue 2026-12-08 10:00–10:45 PT
   - Thu 2026-12-10 09:00–09:45 PT

I’ve also linked the HubSpot deal for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/SOL-4721.

Next actions: Lena — please confirm in-scope systems and which artifacts you can share ahead of the kickoff. Marcus / Procurement — please suggest the best contact for contract & PO timing so we can surface any commercial questions in the kickoff rather than blocking the technical review.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Security & Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

Thanks everyone — we can move forward with the proposed minimal scope (prod API + orchestration + auth). Procurement is looped on this thread (procurement@solsticehealth.com) — they’ll own contract and PO cadence.

I attached our current systems inventory for the pilot (solstice-systems-inventory.csv) to give you an initial map. Our legal team will want to review a DPA; please send your standard DPA and any vendor questionnaire answers you can pre-fill.

Kickoff: Thu 2026-12-07 10:00–10:30 PT works for us — Marcus will send a calendar invite. If you need a longer slot (45m) we can extend.

Look forward to the kickoff.
